Subject: Post-call recap: hosting intent synthesis & migration lift plan — AcmeAI

Hi Alex — thanks for taking the call earlier. Quick written recap + where we landed and clear next steps so nothing slips.

TL;DR
- AcmeAI prefers predictable performance for inference with strong auditability; leaning toward Dedicated capacity with a Private VPC overlay for compliance.
- Current migration sources: callbacks from ModelX API (external vendor) + self-hosted LegacyGPU cluster for batch jobs.
- Immediate asks from your side: throughput targets, retention/snooping requirements for logs, and a rough timeline for lift-and-shift.

Notes from the demo/discovery:
- Workload: ~1.2M tokens/day now, expected to 3–4M within 6 months; 99th pct latency requirement ~120ms for 512-token prompts.
- Data sensitivity: mixed PII (customer identifiers) but most payloads are hashed before send; require KMS-backed keying and audit logs retained 1 year.
- Peak bursts: short bursts up to 10x baseline for marketing events; want ability to burst to Hosted for overflow if Dedicated is saturated.
- Migration constraints: legacy cluster uses custom KV-cache and offload patterns; any lift will need a migration window and an ops runbook.

Proposed next actions (please confirm which you want to proceed with):
1) Preferred initial hosting: (A) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) + Private VPC for audit/ingress controls, (B) Hosted API with strict VPC peering + data-handling controls, or (C) Private on-prem package (air-gapped). Please mark A/B/C and any constraints.
2) I attached a draft SOW and a network diagram stub for your infra team to review — can you share who on your side should receive the network diagram?
3) We’ll scope an ops migration plan if you pick Dedicated/Private — includes a pilot lane for non-critical traffic, KV cache migration tests, and a cutover weekend.
4) Pricing ballpark options: we’ll provide a Dedicated reserve quote and a Hosted-burst policy estimate after you confirm expected sustained RPS and token distribution.

Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB); network-diagram.png (PNG, 640KB)

Thanks again — if you confirm preference (A/B/C) and who on infra should review the diagram, I’ll pull together a tailored migration timeline and draft pricing.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks, Mateo — this is helpful and matches our notes. Short answers below and a couple of clarifying questions.

Hosting preference: B -> leaning toward Dedicated capacity + Private VPC (i.e., we want Dedicated GPUs but isolated VPC and customer-managed peering). The main driver is auditability + predictable latency for SLAs.

Why not purely Hosted: We evaluated Hosted for speed of onboarding, but we need KMS control and longer audit retention than standard Hosted defaults; also procurement would prefer a reserved capacity discussion for sustained baseline.

Migration sources:
- ModelX API: we have ~25% of traffic routed through them for certain prompts; want to switch to Redwood as canonical endpoint.
- LegacyGPU cluster: used for nightly batch generation and retrieval —’s a mix of LLM serving and pre/post-processing hooks.

Questions and asks:
1) Can Redwood support a model variant that matches our legacy kv-cache hooks (we can share callouts) or will we need code changes to adapt?
2) Throughput: baseline 60 rps sustained avg, bursts to 600 rps for short periods — do you have a recommended Dedicated sizing for that pattern?
3) Fallback: can we configure automatic burst routing to Hosted and what are SLA/latency implications when bursting?
4) Security: we’ll need SOC2 evidence and a list of data flows for our security questionnaire; please include the network-diagram.png to our infra team.

I asked ops@acmeai.com (cc’d) to share contact for the network review. If you can send the SOW + a Dedicated reserve ballpark and an NDA for procurement to review, that would help.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, AcmeAI
